title: Finite constant groups on projective curve families
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a projective
morphism of finite-type
schemes over a field, with geometric fibre dimensions at most one.
If the order of a finite abelian group $M$ is invertible on $S$,
every higher direct image
$R^qf_*\underline M$ is
constructible.

proof.text: Fix $n=|M|\ge1$ and the morphism $f$. All sheaves and higher direct images in this argument are abelian sheaves on the small etale sites. The source category has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and $f_*$ is additive and left exact by [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-left-exact]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] (2) applies: the $R^qf_*$ are additive functors and give a long exact sequence for every short exact sequence. We prove, by strong induction on $|N|$, that every $R^qf_*\underline N$, $q\ge0$, is constructible for each finite abelian group $N$ whose order divides $n$. For $N=0$, its constant sheaf is zero and every derived image is zero: an additive functor sends the zero identity to zero, so its value on the zero object is a zero object. The zero sheaf is finite constant, hence constructible by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf].

For nonzero $N$, choose $x\ne0$, let $d>1$ be its least positive period, and choose a prime $\ell\mid d$. Division with remainder shows that $a x=0$ exactly when $d\mid a$; hence $y=(d/\ell)x$ has order exactly $\ell$. Thus $H=\langle y\rangle\cong\mathbf F_\ell$ as an additive group. Translation identifies every coset of $H$ with $H$, so counting the disjoint cosets gives $|N|=\ell|Q|$ for $Q=N/H$. Therefore $|Q|<|N|$, and both $\ell$ and $|Q|$ divide $n$. If $n=\ell a$, then $a n^{-1}$ is an inverse to $\ell$ in every local ring of $S$, so $\ell$ is invertible on $S$. This produces $0\to H\to N\to Q\to0$ and is precisely one step of the finite prime-factor filtration in the blueprint; repeating on $Q$ terminates because its cardinality decreases.

The constant presheaves associated with $0\to H\to N\to Q\to0$ are sectionwise short exact. By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] their sheafifications are the associated constant abelian sheaves. The exactness of abelian sheafification in [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] (2) therefore gives $0\to\underline H\to\underline N\to\underline Q\to0$ on $X_{\Et}$. This is the exactness asserted by Stacks 093J (lemma-constant-exact); no splitting as groups is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [thm-fin-projective-curve-constant] to $f$ and $\ell$. Its projectivity, finite-type-over-a-field and geometric-fibre-dimension hypotheses are unchanged, and step 2 supplies the required invertibility. It gives constructibility of all $R^qf_*\underline H$, since the chosen additive isomorphism $H\cong\mathbf F_\ell$ induces an isomorphism of constant abelian sheaves. The inductive hypothesis applies to $Q$ by step 2 and gives constructibility of all $R^qf_*\underline Q$. The induction is simultaneous in every degree, so it supplies the terms in degrees $q$ and $q+1$, and in degree $q-1$ when $q>0$, needed below; the degree $-1$ boundary is treated separately in step 6.

Set $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n$. Each of $H,N,Q$ is killed by $n$: for any element $z$ of a finite group $P$ of order dividing $n$, its cyclic subgroup has size equal to its least positive period $e$, and counting its cosets gives $e\mid|P|\mid n$, hence $nz=0$. This equality passes to constant sheaves by sheafification. Additivity from [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] (2) gives $n\,\mathrm{id}_{R^qf_*\underline P}=R^qf_*(n\,\mathrm{id}_{\underline P})=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaves-killed-by-n-zmod-modules] (2),(3), all these sheaves have unique $\Lambda_S$-module structures and every abelian map between them is $\Lambda_S$-linear. A constructible abelian sheaf killed by $n$ is constructible with this module structure: on each stratum of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf], additivity of inverse image in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] preserves the equation $n\,\mathrm{id}=0$. A local constant finite group model is therefore killed by $n$: discard empty members of the trivializing cover and evaluate at a geometric point, using the canonical group identification of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk]; give that group its integer-multiplication action modulo $n$. Its constant module sheaf is obtained by sheafifying this action on the constant presheaf; thus its underlying abelian sheaf is the chosen constant abelian model by [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The local isomorphisms are linear by clause (3) of the same killed-by-$n$ node. They are exactly the finite constant module models required by [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Conversely, forgetting scalars in such local module models gives the abelian constructibility condition. Thus the sheaves obtained in step 4 are constructible $\Lambda_S$-module sheaves, without changing their underlying abelian higher direct images. The module inverse image to a stratum has this same underlying abelian inverse image by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] (2). Thus the local-model comparison also applies to the module restrictions appearing in the definition.

source.place: Definition 03RW (definition-constructible), parts (2),(3); elementary comparison of local models using the cited killed-by-n lemma

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to step 3, with the hypotheses checked in step 1. For a fixed $q\ge0$, write $A=R^qf_*\underline H$, $B=R^qf_*\underline N$, $C=R^qf_*\underline Q$ and $D=R^{q+1}f_*\underline H$. For $q>0$ put $T=R^{q-1}f_*\underline Q$; for $q=0$ put $T=0$, using the initial $0\to f_*\underline H\to f_*\underline N$ of the long exact sequence. Its exact segment $T\xrightarrow u A\xrightarrow v B\xrightarrow w C\xrightarrow z D$ gives $0\to\operatorname{coker}u\to B\to\ker z\to0$: $\ker v=\operatorname{im}u$ makes the map from $A/\operatorname{im}u$ injective with image $\operatorname{im}v=\ker w$, and $\operatorname{im}w=\ker z$ makes the map to $\ker z$ surjective. These are also the module kernel and cokernel and a module short exact sequence: by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise quotients with inherited scalar action, so their underlying abelian objects are precisely those just computed. All arrows are linear by step 5.

source.place: Tag 015B, lemma-higher-derived-functors (1),(2); elementary image/kernel calculation from the exact segment

proof.text: The ring $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n$ is finite and commutative, including $n=1$. In step 6, $T,A,C,D$ are constructible $\Lambda_S$-module sheaves by steps 4 and 5 (and $T=0$ when $q=0$). Apply [thm-constructible-serre] (1) to $u:T\to A$ and $z:C\to D$: their cokernel and kernel are constructible. Clause (2) applied to the short exact sequence of step 6 then makes $B$ constructible as a $\Lambda_S$-module sheaf. Forgetting the scalar action in its finite constant local models gives constructibility as an abelian sheaf by [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] and [def-weil-pbc-constructible-abelian-sheaf]. This finishes the induction for every $q\ge0$. Taking $N=M$ proves the item. If negative degrees are included in the notation, they vanish: use an injective resolution concentrated in nonnegative degrees in the definition [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], whose image under $f_*$ is still concentrated in those degrees.
